challenges.name: install-scripts-quiz
challenges.title: Which install scripts run?
challenges.description: Two pieces of CodeDev's install pipeline: what --ignore-scripts plus a reviewed rebuild list does to a new package's postinstall, and whether an allowlisted name may run a new version's script.

questions.explanation: True. --ignore-scripts stops npm ci from running any lifecycle script, from every dependency and from the project itself, so the new package's postinstall never runs. npm rebuild then runs the install scripts only of the packages named on its command line, which here come from the reviewed allowlist. The misconception is that blocking scripts must break native modules: they still build, but only the ones someone reviewed. The new package's script should still appear in the job's report as blocked, so the PR author knows to ask for a review if it is really needed.

False. The review covered the code of sharp 0.34.4, identified by its integrity hash. 0.34.5 is new code from the registry, and a patch release is exactly what an attacker who took over a maintainer's account would publish: in 2025 several widely used npm packages shipped malicious patch versions that way, some running their payload from an install script. Pinning the allowlist to name, version and integrity turns every version bump of a package with install scripts into a small, explicit review: diff the scripts, then add the new entry. The misconception is to trust a name; trust belongs to reviewed bytes.

challenges.name: spot-the-ai-mistake-install-scripts
challenges.title: Spot the AI Mistake: install scripts allowed by default
challenges.description: CodeDev's CI ran npm ci --ignore-scripts and then npm rebuild for the packages that planInstallScripts allowed. After sharp was added the build failed, and an AI assistant was asked: "make the CI install step faster and stop the native module build failing". It merged the steps into npm ci --foreground-scripts --unsafe-perm (the team has reverted that line) and rewrote planInstallScripts; the build is green and the public tests pass. Fix planInstallScripts(lock, allowlist) so that it follows CodeDev's install policy and returns { run, blocked }. Scripts that count, when present with a non-empty value: preinstall, install, postinstall for registry packages; the same plus prepare for git dependencies (resolved starts with "git+", "git://" or "github:"); prepare of a registry package never runs and is not reported. A script runs only when the allowlist has an entry with the same name, the same version and the same non-empty integrity as the package. Every other script is blocked with the first reason that applies: "git_dependency" (a git dependency, never allowlisted), "not_allowlisted" (no entry with this name), "version_mismatch" (entries for this name, none with this exact version; a range such as "^0.25.0" matches no version), "integrity_mismatch" (an entry with this name and version, but none with the package's integrity, or the integrity is ""). run items are { package: "<name>@<version>", script }, blocked items add reason. Order: packages in lockfile order, then scripts in the order preinstall, install, postinstall, prepare. The runner reads { lock, allowlist } and prints the plan as JSON.
hints: What happens to a package that nobody has reviewed: which branch of the if does it take? Then ask the same question for a package whose name was reviewed at another version.

Look at the constant next to the comment that explains why the build broke, and at what `reviewed` contains: names only. Then compare INSTALL_SCRIPTS with the scripts npm runs for a git dependency, and check how a git dependency could ever match an allowlist entry pinned to an integrity hash.

A similar case on other data: allowlist [{ name: "canvas", version: "2.11.2", integrity: "sha512-AAA" }]. canvas 2.11.2 with integrity sha512-AAA and an install script: it runs. canvas 2.11.3: blocked, version_mismatch. canvas 2.11.2 with sha512-BBB: blocked, integrity_mismatch. A package resolved from "git+ssh://git@github.com/acme/tool.git#c0ffee" with a prepare script: blocked, git_dependency. A registry package with only prepare and test scripts: nothing to run, nothing to report.
